classification.difficultyReason: Interpret multiple true and reverse bearings to derive a triangle, apply the sine rule and construct a perpendicular to a course for closest approach. The last unsignposted geometric connection determines the Mastery demand.

content.prompt: A ship is sailing on a bearing of $350^\circ\mathrm{T}$. At 2 p.m., the bearing from the ship to North Cape Light is $080^\circ\mathrm{T}$ and the bearing from the ship to South Light is $105^\circ\mathrm{T}$. It is clear from a map that the bearing from South Light to North Cape Light is $355^\circ\mathrm{T}$, and they are $1.5$ km apart.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Draw a diagram using $A$ for the point that the bearings were taken from the ship, $N$ for North Cape Light and $S$ for South Light. Clearly label all bearings and true north directions.

answer.short: Diagram showing $A\to N:080^\circ\mathrm{T}$, $A\to S:105^\circ\mathrm{T}$, $S\to N:355^\circ\mathrm{T}$, the ship’s course $350^\circ\mathrm{T}$ and $NS=1.5\text{ km}$, with true north arrows.
answer.worked: Measure bearings clockwise from true north. Draw $AN$ on bearing $080^\circ\mathrm{T}$ and $AS$ on bearing $105^\circ\mathrm{T}$. From $S$, draw $SN$ on bearing $355^\circ\mathrm{T}$ and label $NS=1.5\text{ km}$. The ship’s course through $A$ is $10^\circ$ west of north.

spec.description: Bearing-derived triangle with north arrows at A and S, clockwise bearing arcs and the ship’s course.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Draw $\triangle ANS$, indicating the angles and side lengths that are known.

answer.worked:
The reverse bearing from $S$ to $A$ is $285^\circ\mathrm{T}$.
$$\begin{align*}\angle NAS&=105^\circ-80^\circ\\\angle NAS&=25^\circ\\\angle ASN&=355^\circ-285^\circ\\\angle ASN&=70^\circ\\\angle ANS&=180^\circ-25^\circ-70^\circ\\\angle ANS&=85^\circ\end{align*}$$
Label $NS=1.5\text{ km}$.

spec.description: Separate triangle ANS with all three interior angles and the known lighthouse separation.
spec.mathematics: Angles at A,N,S are 25°,85°,70° respectively; NS=1.5 km.

children.label: c
children.prompt: Find the distance from the 2 p.m. position of the ship to the North Cape Light, to the nearest metre.

answer.worked:
Using the sine rule in $\triangle ANS$:
$$\begin{align*}\frac{AN}{\sin70^\circ}&=\frac{1.5}{\sin25^\circ}\\AN&=\frac{1.5\sin70^\circ}{\sin25^\circ}\text{ km}\\AN&\approx3335\text{ m}\quad\text{(nearest metre)}\end{align*}$$

children.label: d
children.prompt: If the ship has maintained a constant course, find, to the nearest metre, the closest it came to South Light.

inlines.text: Use the perpendicular distance from South Light to the ship’s course.

answer.worked:
Let $H$ be the foot of the perpendicular from $S$ to the ship’s course. The reverse course from $A$ has bearing $170^\circ\mathrm{T}$, so $\angle SAH=170^\circ-105^\circ=65^\circ$. The closest approach occurred before 2 p.m.

Using the sine rule, then right-triangle trigonometry:
$$\begin{align*}AS&=\frac{1.5\sin85^\circ}{\sin25^\circ}\text{ km}\\SH&=AS\sin65^\circ\\SH&=\frac{1.5\sin85^\circ\sin65^\circ}{\sin25^\circ}\text{ km}\\SH&\approx3205\text{ m}\quad\text{(nearest metre)}\end{align*}$$
